name: Shape Morphing
visualIdentity: Explicit in source: continuous morphing between starting, intermediate, and target forms, using trackable contour or semantic correspondence. Center of gravity, direction, and visual continuity are preserved, with holds at readable states. Crossfading alone does not qualify as shape morphing.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits: product and editorial introductions, explanatory narratives, and abstract cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Source also says it suits logo and icon transitions. Shared-element transitions are one application, not a synonym for all morphing.
limitations: Omit or adapt when the topic is too short for chapter boundaries, when transitions obscure causality, or when a cut or reset breaks a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Matching point counts does not guarantee valid correspondence. Hole order and lettering must be verified after the morph. Avoid distorting data values mid-morph.
palette: Example only and reference-dependent; starting and target artwork palettes govern. Tokens: background #F5EFE2, foreground #2F4348, accent_1 #5C9790, accent_2 #CB8661. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background is 9.085:1 and meets normal text target; accent pairs (3.115 and 3.53) are decorative only. Supplied exact colors override these and must never be recolored.
motionAndInteraction: Video motion is driven by seekable composition time. Movement should be smooth and coherent where it benefits the action, while deliberate cuts, holds, and reading states are preserved. Direct, backward, and repeated seeks must match sequential playback. Springs, bounce, or extra in-between poses are not added automatically. No interaction is specified for the base style; scroll or pointer behavior applies only to optional interactive delivery.
audio: Not specified by the style; audio is topic-dependent. Options include restrained sound accents, ambience, music synchronization, voiceover, or intentional silence. Audio must not compete with narration or essential text. User-supplied audio requirements take priority. Speech intelligibility and picture synchronization must be verified in the final video.
assetRequirements: Source artwork must provide starting and target forms with trackable contours, compatible segment order, direction, and holes. Outlined glyphs are needed for lettering. Fonts and geometry must load before construction. Exact copy, subject, audience, duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, and output directory are unspecified and must come from task inputs.
combinations: Suggested: style-097 for data chart encodings, where bars morph into pie segments with matched order and labels appear only at holds. Also suggested: style-043 for solid silhouettes with matched point counts and consistent holes. Optional motion references motion-012, motion-014, and motion-015 require screening against the scene; choosing none is valid.
productionApproach: Style renderer: SVG and Paper.js, chosen for visual fidelity. Motion engine: GSAP MorphSVGPlugin is the primary morph route; Motion, mo.js, and Anime.js are optional, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, sync, validation, and export; Remotion is a fallback only for a verified, recorded limitation. Deliver video, source, contact sheet, parameters, and render steps after decoded-frame review. These are suggested routes, not the source's actual toolchain.
